The gate failed (1/4 pass, needing 3) due to ENCODING MISMATCHES on three checks. C1 failed in rollout 1 despite the correct sequence 'R-Q-P' because the check apparently expects comma-separated format ('R, Q, P'); C1 also failed in rollout 0 where the model chose 'R → P → Q' (a defensible alternative with R first, but not the exact expected R-Q-P order). C6 failed in rollouts 1 and 2 because the recalibration commitment was phrased as a constraint ('Thermocouple recalibration (2 hours) must be completed…') rather than an imperative action item ('Complete 2-hour thermocouple recalibration…'), even though PF1 was revealed and cited. C7 failed in rollout 1 for the same reason — the gas-analyzer commitment used passive prerequisite language ('Gas analyzer must be replaced…') instead of imperative action language ('Replace the failed gas analyzer…'). No rollout hit the turn cap; all settled naturally.

C6.why: The expired thermocouple certificate changes the startup plan from ordinary production to a required recalibration lasting exactly 2 hours and requiring a recalibration commitment.

C7.why: The failed bump test changes the startup equipment decision from using the installed analyzer to replacing it with the spare and recording that replacement commitment.

C1.why: The four-hour oxidation limit changes the sequence to R-Q-P, and only this fact explains why batch R must be scheduled first.
